_doc: Every token on a real tradition id in references/_tradition_signatures.json, classed. Read by scripts/check_signature_tokens.js, which fails on a signature token this file does not class, so a new token - cultural or not - cannot slip in unclassified. Classes: 'cultural' - claims the tradition belongs to, descends from, or is shaped by a specific culture, people, place, language, religion or rite, or a named cultural tradition (ethnonyms and places, languages, specific religions and liturgies, named lineages such as gagaku-foundational or samba-foundation, culture-specific form names, and materials that name a place, maker or people rather than a species); every (tradition, cultural token) pair must carry a ruling in references/_signature_rulings.json. 'style' - a cross-cultural genre or idiom descriptor (jazz, funk-derived, rock-context), a Western art-music period or training word (baroque-*, classical, romantic), a generic function word naming no specific religion (devotional, liturgical, ceremonial), a species-only material (sitka-spruce, keyaki) or a gear line; recorded here, not ruled per pair and not gated beyond classification. 'sonic' - a sound, technique, texture, form, affect, instrument, material or production word. Where a token is ambiguous between cultural and style it is cultural only if it names a specific people, place, language, religion or named cultural tradition.
_fields: class: cultural | style | sonic. kind (cultural, style): ethnonym-place | religion-rite | named-lineage | material-provenance - what the claim is about. group (style): genre-idiom | art-music-period | generic-function | species-material | gear-lineage. gloss: what the token claims. note (optional): why a borderline token sits in its class.

African-craft.gloss: claims an African craft / instrument-making lineage

African-derived.gloss: claims derivation from African musical traditions (Africa or the African diaspora)

African-traditional.gloss: claims the tradition is, or descends from, traditional African music

Hindu-ritual.gloss: claims a Hindu ritual / devotional context

Italian-baroque.gloss: claims Italian Baroque lineage (Monteverdi / Corelli / Vivaldi school)
Italian-baroque.note: kept cultural: names a place (Italy) on top of the period; the bare baroque-* period words are style

Middle-Eastern.gloss: claims Middle-Eastern lineage (Arab, Persian, Turkish, Levantine sphere)

Turkish-makam-base.gloss: claims a Turkish / Ottoman makam modal basis

aleke.gloss: names aleke, the Guianese Maroon popular-music genre

ambient.note: texture word (on ambient traditions only); no cultural origin claim

anent.gloss: names anent, the Shuar intimate ritual song

arabic-maqam.gloss: claims the Arabic maqam modal system

baroque-pitch.gloss: claims European Baroque pitch practice (A=415 etc.)

baroque-setup.gloss: claims a European Baroque instrument set-up

blues-derived.gloss: claims derivation from the blues (African-American genre lineage)
blues-derived.note: genre-derivation claim of the same shape as funk-derived (style); blues family (bluesy / blues-inflected / blues-shouter are style). Unlike gospel-rooted it names no church or religion

blues-shouter.gloss: claims the blues-shouter vocal lineage (Kansas City / jump-blues shouters)

bluesy.gloss: blues idiom adjective (implies blues lineage); blue-note feel reading possible

bosavi.gloss: names the Bosavi (Kaluli) people / Mount Bosavi, Papua New Guinea

cante-jondo.gloss: names cante jondo, the deep song of Andalusian flamenco

celtic.gloss: claims a Celtic lineage (Irish, Scottish, Welsh, Breton, Cornish, Manx, Galician/Asturian)

ceremonial.gloss: claims a ceremonial / ritual function (civic or religious)

chant-foundational.note: vocal form (chant) found across cultures; names no religion

chesols.gloss: names chesols, the Palauan solo-chant genre

chewa.gloss: names the Chewa people (Malawi, Zambia, Mozambique)

chukchi.gloss: names the Chukchi people (Chukotka, NE Siberia)

classical.gloss: Western art-music (classical) lineage as the catalog uses it; generic "art music" register reading possible

classical-jazz.gloss: claims a classical-jazz (swing-era / mainstream jazz) lineage
classical-jazz.note: jazz family: names a jazz idiom (swing-era / mainstream), no people, place or religion

classical-radif.gloss: claims a classical radif basis (the canonical repertoire of Persian classical music)

classical-trained.gloss: claims Western classical (conservatory) training; generic register reading possible

congregation-loud.gloss: implies a worshipping congregation (church / religious assembly) setting; loudness reading possible

court-ceremonial.gloss: claims a royal / princely court ceremonial context

cremonese-pre-1750.gloss: claims Cremonese (Cremona, Italy) pre-1750 violin-making lineage

dakpa.gloss: names the Dakpa subgroup of the Banda people (Central African Republic)

dark-romantic.note: affect adjective used across cultures (tango, bambuco, emo, doom); not the Romantic era

dastgah.gloss: names the Persian dastgah modal system

devotional.gloss: claims a religious-devotional function or context (no religion named; sonic "devout affect" reading possible)

dhrupad-suited.gloss: claims fit with dhrupad, the Hindustani (North Indian) classical genre

dub-friendly.gloss: claims affinity with dub (Jamaican studio lineage); affordance reading possible

eucalyptus-tetrodonta.gloss: Darwin stringybark, native to northern Australia (termite-hollowed yidaki wood)

european-alpine.gloss: claims European Alpine lineage (Austria, Switzerland, Bavaria, Tyrol)

european-orchestral.note: kept cultural: names a place (Europe); ambiguous tokens stay cultural when they name a place

fang.gloss: names the Fang people (Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Cameroon)

folk.note: register word used across cultures in this catalog (country, tango, jibaro, mande_griot ...); names no culture

folk-tradition.note: register word used across cultures (bluegrass, gnawa, hiragasy ...); names no culture

folkloric.note: register word used across cultures; names no culture

french-musette-ready.gloss: claims affinity with French (Parisian) bal-musette accordion style

french-renaissance.note: kept cultural: names a place (France) on top of the period

funk-derived.gloss: claims derivation from funk (African-American genre lineage, late 1960s on)

funk-friendly.gloss: claims affinity with funk; affordance reading possible

funky.gloss: funk idiom adjective (implies funk lineage); generic groove-feel reading possible

gaelic-tradition.gloss: claims a Gaelic-language (Irish or Scottish Gaelic) tradition

gagaku-foundational.gloss: claims a foundation in gagaku, the Japanese imperial court music

galeazzi-1791.gloss: cites Francesco Galeazzi's 1791 Italian violin treatise (named Italian source)

gamaka-ornamentation.gloss: names gamaka, Indian (esp. Carnatic) oscillating ornamentation

gospel-friendly.gloss: claims affinity with the gospel (Protestant church-song) idiom; affordance reading possible

gospel-pentecostal.note: kept cultural: names a specific religious movement (Pentecostalism), unlike the generic gospel-runs / gospel-friendly idiom words

gospel-rooted.gloss: claims roots in gospel music (African-American / Southern Protestant church song)
gospel-rooted.note: kept cultural: read as a claim of descent from Black-church / Southern Protestant church song, unlike the idiom words gospel-runs / gospel-friendly, which are style

gospel-runs.gloss: claims gospel-church vocal runs (names the African-American Protestant gospel idiom)

haida.gloss: names the Haida people (Haida Gwaii, Pacific Northwest)

hard-rock-maple.note: tonewood species (Acer saccharum), not the hard-rock genre

haunted-romantic.note: affect adjective; not the Romantic era

hocket.note: general technique term (interlocking single notes) used cross-culturally

iberian-celtic.gloss: claims an Iberian-Celtic lineage (compound: Iberian peninsula + Celtic, e.g. Galicia/Asturias)

italian-alpine-spruce.gloss: claims Italian Alpine spruce tonewood (place of origin)

jazz-friendly.gloss: claims affinity with the jazz idiom (African-American lineage); affordance reading possible

jazz-improvisation.note: jazz family (jazz / jazz-influenced / jazz-friendly / scat are style)

jazz-trained.note: jazz family (jazz / jazz-influenced / jazz-friendly / scat are style)

kargyraa.gloss: names kargyraa, the Tuvan low throat-singing style

katajjaq.gloss: names katajjaq, the Inuit throat-singing game

katta-ashula.gloss: names katta ashula, the Fergana Valley (Uzbek / Tajik) vocal art

kawina.gloss: names kawina, the Surinamese Creole song genre

keyaki.gloss: Japanese-language name for zelkova wood (taiko shells)

khoomei.gloss: names khoomei, Tuvan / Mongolian throat singing

khyal.gloss: names khyal, the Hindustani classical vocal genre

koryak.gloss: names the Koryak people (Kamchatka, NE Siberia)

kriti-form.gloss: names kriti, the Carnatic (South Indian) composition form

kurinuki-construction.gloss: Japanese-language term for single-log hollowed taiko construction
kurinuki-construction.note: kept cultural: the Japanese-language name of a Japanese taiko-making technique (single-log hollowing, kurinuki-daiko), not a species

lakalaka.gloss: names lakalaka, the Tongan sung-speech-dance genre

late-Romantic-onward.gloss: claims descent from the late-Romantic era of European art music (late 19th c. on)

late-baroque.note: baroque-* period qualifier (style, like every baroque-* word)

linda.gloss: names the Linda subgroup of the Banda people (Central African Republic)

liturgical.gloss: claims use in, or descent from, formal religious liturgy (no religion named)

lyon.gloss: claims Lyon (France) gut strings (historic string type named for Lyon)

madi.gloss: names the Ma'di people (Uganda / South Sudan)

maltese-ghana.gloss: names ghana, the Maltese folk-song genre

marching-bateria.gloss: Portuguese/Spanish 'bateria' (drum section); read as a samba-school bateria it is a Brazilian lineage claim

mari.gloss: names the Mari people (Volga-Finnic, Mari El, Russia)

marine-band-tradition.gloss: names the Hohner Marine Band harmonica lineage (German diatonic harmonica, 1896); also readable as a military-band tradition
marine-band-tradition.note: names a harmonica model line (Hohner Marine Band), i.e. a piece of gear, not a people, place, language, religion or named cultural tradition; same footing as vintage-steinway

maroon.gloss: names the Maroon peoples (e.g. Guianese Maroons of Suriname / French Guiana)

metal-context.gloss: claims a heavy-metal context (UK/US genre lineage)

metallic.note: timbre descriptor (also on metal-vessel/tin instruments), not the metal genre

mid-baroque-period.note: baroque-* period qualifier (style, like every baroque-* word)

monastic-chant.gloss: claims monastic (religious-order) chant lineage (no religion named)

mwinoghe.gloss: names mwinoghe, the northern Malawian drum-dance

nampet.gloss: names nampet, the Shuar festive song genre

north-australia.gloss: claims northern-Australian Aboriginal origin (Arnhem Land, Daly/Wadeye, Kimberley)

northeast-arnhem.gloss: claims Northeast Arnhem Land (Yolngu, Australia) origin

norway-spruce.gloss: tonewood species Picea abies; its common name carries a place (Norway)

ob-ugric.gloss: names the Ob-Ugric peoples (Khanty and Mansi, western Siberia)

oral-tradition.note: transmission mode, universal; names no culture

overtone-singing.note: general technique (not a named culture-specific style)

pan-African.gloss: claims membership of a pan-African (continental Africa + diaspora) musical sphere

parixara.gloss: names parixara, the Makushi-Wapichana song-dance (Guiana highlands)

pistoy.gloss: claims Pistoy basses (historic gut-string type named for Pistoia, Italy)

pop.note: register word (popular music); names no culture

qawwali.gloss: names qawwali, the Sufi devotional song of South Asia (Chishti lineage)

raga-bound.gloss: claims organisation by raga (the South Asian modal system)

rock-context.gloss: claims a rock-music context (Anglo-American genre lineage)
rock-context.note: rock family (rock / folk-rock / metal-context are style)

romantic.gloss: Romantic-era (19th-c. European art-music) lineage; affect reading "romantic" possible

sacred-Latin.gloss: claims a Latin-rite (Roman Catholic, Latin-language) sacred lineage

sacred-traditional.gloss: claims a sacred (religious) traditional function (no religion named)

samba-batería.gloss: claims the samba-school bateria (Brazilian samba percussion) lineage

sao-tome.gloss: names Sao Tome (Sao Tome and Principe)

scat.gloss: names jazz scat singing (implies jazz lineage)

selknam.gloss: names the Selk'nam people (Tierra del Fuego)

shuar.gloss: names the Shuar people (Ecuadorian / Peruvian Amazon)

sitka-spruce.gloss: tonewood species Picea sitchensis; its common name carries a place (Sitka, Alaska)

southern-Italian.gloss: claims southern-Italian lineage (Naples, Sicily, Calabria, Apulia/Salento)

sprechgesang-vocal.note: loanword technique term in general use (speech-song), like glissando/tremolo

sufi-mystical.gloss: claims a Sufi (Islamic mystical) lineage or character

sugarbag-beeswax.gloss: Australian Aboriginal English 'sugarbag' (native-bee) wax for the yidaki mouthpiece

sygyt.gloss: names sygyt, the Tuvan whistle-register throat-singing style

tajik-falak.gloss: names falak, the Tajik (Pamir / Badakhshan) mountain-song genre

tarab.gloss: names tarab, the Arab aesthetic of musical ecstasy (Egyptian/Levantine/Iraqi art music)

tibesti.gloss: names the Tibesti massif region (Chad/Libya; Teda-Tubu peoples)

turkmen-bagshy.gloss: names the Turkmen bagshy bardic lineage

tuvan-whistle.gloss: claims Tuvan throat-singing lineage (sygyt whistle register)

udmurt-krez.gloss: names krez, the North Udmurt vocal genre (Udmurt people, Volga-Ural)

urban-Greek.gloss: claims urban-Greek lineage (rebetiko/laiko sphere: Piraeus, Athens, Smyrna)

val-di-fiemme.gloss: claims Val di Fiemme (Trentino, Italy) spruce tonewood

valley-tonga.gloss: names the Valley (Gwembe) Tonga people (Zambia / Zimbabwe)

venice-catlin.gloss: claims Venice catlin gut strings (historic Venetian string type)

vintage-steinway.note: kept sonic: a piano make names no people, place, language, religion or cultural lineage

wayapi.gloss: names the Wayapi people (French Guiana / Amapa, Brazil)

yupik.gloss: names the Yup'ik / Yupik peoples (Alaska, Chukotka)

zelkova.gloss: Zelkova serrata (Japanese keyaki) wood; listed as culture-bearing in the prior audit
